correctness.rationale: The finite affine partition covers every canonical fundamental-domain point and yields greedy m-adic digits after merging two labels. On the simultaneous full-measure equidistributed-orbit set, its split-label frequency is theta/m, recovering the neutral factor. Product entropy is log m. For any m-symbol generator, subadditivity plus maximum entropy forces every n-word to have probability m^{-n}; the induced factor is Bernoulli and ergodic, contradicting the fixed theta observable. The proof works for all integers m>=2, no numerical extrapolation. Boundaries are finitely piecewise affine including toral seams.

value.rationale: The minimum smooth-symbol cardinality is a natural coding invariant for a basic infinite family of neutral–expanding toral maps. An explicit piecewise affine optimum at one alphabet symbol above entropy sharpness is a motivated classification at the boundary between strict contraction obstruction and expansion. Frequency coding of an invariant neutral coordinate within one m-adic digit cylinder supplies the nontrivial constructive mechanism; the entropy-rigidity lower bound proves optimality. It is stronger than a nonoptimal coordinate-comparison code and not a bare entropy corollary.
